patch.objective: Ensuring value-based delivery: identifying value components, prioritizing work by value and feedback, and verifying a benefits-tracking system is in place
secondaryObjectives: Evaluating project status: developing project metrics, ensuring artifacts are created and kept accessible, and communicating status

sources.cite: PMI, Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline, July 2026 Update: People 33%, Process 41%, Business Environment 26%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a training provider (the course seed cites PMI's own copy). Relevant text: Domain II Task 3 'Help ensure value-based delivery' ('Prioritize work based on value and stakeholder feedback'; 'Assess opportunities to deliver value incrementally'); Task 8 'Plan and manage schedule' ('Baseline a project schedule'; 'Analyze schedule variation'); Domain III Task 3 'Manage and control changes' ('Execute the change control process'); Task 4 'Remove impediments and manage issues' ('Evaluate the impact of impediments'; 'Recognize when a risk becomes an issue'); Task 5 'Plan and manage risk'; Task 8 'Evaluate external business environment changes' ('Assess and prioritize the impact on project scope/backlog based on changes in the external business environment'). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Increment: 'Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint'; 'an Increment may be delivered to stakeholders prior to the end of the Sprint'; 'The Sprint Review should never be considered a gate to releasing value.'

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Definition of Done: 'If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review. Instead, it returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration.' Sprints are fixed length.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Sprint Review: 'The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations'; 'a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation'; the Product Backlog may be adjusted to meet new opportunities.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Sprint Retrospective: 'The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness'; the most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible and may be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint.
